hypothesis: Broadcom historical issuer guidance accuracy provides an empirical prior strong enough to justify at least 78.70986999% probability on the 10% rather than 0% post-FY2028 AVGO growth branch.
capital_allocation_importance: The canonical AVGO versus NVDA comparison requires 78.70986999% probability on the 10% post-FY2028 growth branch merely to match NVDA. This run tests whether Broadcom's own historical guidance record can legitimately supply that conviction instead of inventing a probability.

precommitted_decision_rule.USE: A directly comparable issuer-history base rate supports at least 78.70986999% probability for the required multi-year growth outcome.
precommitted_decision_rule.CONDITION: Issuer history is directionally supportive but horizon or identity differs materially from the FY2029-FY2031 growth event.
precommitted_decision_rule.REJECT: Issuer history cannot validly support the 78.70986999% multi-year growth probability, or a naive mapping would conflate short-horizon guidance accuracy with long-horizon growth persistence.
precommitted_decision_rule.UNVERIFIED: Point-in-time guidance or realized revenue identity cannot be verified from issuer sources.

benchmark_comparison.benchmark: 78.70986999% probability hurdle from the canonical 0%/10% AVGO post-FY2028 growth comparison.
benchmark_comparison.simple_alternative: Naively use Broadcom's Q4 revenue-guidance hit rate as the probability prior.
benchmark_comparison.result: Broadcom realized revenue met or exceeded the Q3-issued Q4 revenue guidance in all six verified FY2020-FY2025 observations, but that 100% one-quarter guidance hit rate is not the same event as sustaining at least 10% total-revenue CAGR through FY2029-FY2031.
benchmark_comparison.interpretation: The historical record supports short-horizon execution credibility, not a 78.71% probability of three-year post-outlook growth persistence. Mapping the hit rate directly would be a horizon and target-identity error.

method.look_ahead_control: Each guidance value is taken from the issuer's Q3 release before the corresponding Q4 result; actual revenue is taken from the later issuer Q4/FY release.
method.simple_strategy_comparison: Compare the canonical 78.71% hurdle with a naive issuer-guidance hit-rate prior, then reject the mapping if event horizon/identity differs.
method.no_silent_mapping: A one-quarter revenue-guidance beat is not converted into a probability for a three-year CAGR event.

risk_metrics.reason: This is a point-in-time forecast-calibration study, not a realized return-series backtest.

primary_sources: Broadcom Q3 FY2020 and Q4 FY2020 results
Broadcom Q3 FY2021 and Q4 FY2021 results
Broadcom Q3 FY2022 and Q4 FY2022 results
Broadcom Q3 FY2023 and Q4 FY2023 results
Broadcom Q3 FY2024 and Q4 FY2024 results
Broadcom Q3 FY2025 and Q4 FY2025 results

decision.reason: The verified issuer history is impressively accurate at a one-quarter horizon, but it does not observe the FY2029-FY2031 multi-year event required by the valuation model. Therefore it cannot supply the 78.70986999% probability without an invalid horizon/identity substitution.
decision.portfolio_implication: Do not upgrade AVGO relative to NVDA by treating Broadcom's historical quarterly guidance hit rate as the probability of sustained post-FY2028 growth. Keep the 78.71% figure as a required conviction hurdle, not an empirical prior.

implementation.usage_rule: Never substitute short-horizon guidance hit rates for long-horizon growth probabilities unless target identity and horizon are comparable.

remaining_uncertainty: A valid empirical prior requires comparable multi-year Broadcom growth transitions or a broader, explicitly comparable cohort of custom-AI/semiconductor growth regimes; six one-quarter guidance observations cannot identify the FY2029-FY2031 probability distribution.
next_hypothesis: A point-in-time historical base rate of Broadcom three-year forward revenue CAGR following high-growth regimes, compared with semiconductor peers, can bound the probability that FY2029-FY2031 total-revenue CAGR remains at least 10%.
